note: M19's capability document panel — the mock's `sh-readme` sheet at :3953-4079.
TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS DECIDE MOST OF THIS FILE, AND BOTH ARE DECLARED HERE.
1. THIS SURFACE HAS NO `.v-*` FRAME. Every board and the Settings window carry `v-ideal` /
`v-empty` blocks, and mock_fidelity.py passed `v-<state>` to the affordance census as a
literal. A sheet carries its whole state in one element, so the census exited 3 at
`#sh-readme has no .v-ideal block` and this surface could not be measured at all. The
manifest key `stateFrames` is the capability that fixes it: a value beginning with `#` is
an id rather than a class, and the default is still `v-<state>`, so servers, settings and
the selftest's own fixture are byte-identical in behaviour. Verified by running all six
existing censuses before and after: 87 / 6 / 8 / 6 and 52 / 4, unchanged.
2. ONE STATE, BECAUSE THE MOCK DRAWS ONE FRAME. The panel's own designed states — a tab the
capability published nothing for, a source that has not answered, and a source that
cannot — are built and unit-tested (CapabilityDocumentSheetTests) and are NOT measured
here, because there is no mock frame to measure them against and mock-affordances.py exits
3 rather than inventing one. That is a real gap in this surface's coverage and it is stated
rather than left to be inferred from a states list of length one.
THE CENSUS GREW, AND IT GREW FOR EVERY SURFACE.
Five of the census's declared kinds knew only the boards' spelling. `.callout` counted and
`<blockquote>` did not; `.trow` counted and `<li>` did not; `.codeblock` counted and `<pre>`
did not; a `.c` inside `.thead` counted and `<th>` did not; and `badge` — one of the M23
brief's own words — had no rule at all, so the shields this item exists to draw were invisible
to the instrument meant to check them. The rules now read both spellings. Measured before and
after over all six existing frames: no existing count moved, so this is additive rather than a
re-basing. This surface's census went 24 to 51.
VOUCHED_CONTROLS gained five pairings for the same reason, which is the case `D-m23-h` in
ORCHESTRATOR.md's deferred register names: the first surface to pair a kind reads it as a
finding until somebody vouches for it deliberately.
SIX DECLARED DIVERGENCES. EVERY CITATION OPENS WITH `Dn · `, following settings.layers.json's
rule, so the split is countable off the generated ledger's own citation column:
F='| \(absent\|divergent\|extra\|extra-cited\|unclassified\) |'
grep -c "$F" planning/fidelity/readme.ledger.md
grep "$F" planning/fidelity/readme.ledger.md | grep -c '| D[0-9] ·'
grep -o '| D[0-9] ·' planning/fidelity/readme.ledger.md | sort | uniq -c
1. THE MOCK IS A TAB SET AND THE BUILD RENDERS ONE TAB. Owner: nobody — it is the conversion.
All three tab bodies sit in the mock's DOM at once with `hidden` deciding which is visible,
so the census inventories the read me, the changelog and the capability list together. The
build renders the selected tab and nothing else, which is what a tab is. Every affordance
belonging to the changelog and capabilities documents is therefore absent from this run.
Identical in shape to settings.layers.json's D3, and closing it would mean rendering three
documents at once.
2. THE THREE ACTIONS THE PANEL CANNOT PERFORM. Owner: M18, which owns the sheet inventory and
the install flow. The mock draws `What changed…`, `Install…` and `Update to 1.5.0`; this
panel can perform none of the three. `CapabilityDocumentSheet.actions` is the seam they
pass through and the measured render supplies none, because a button drawn here would be a
press that does nothing — DESIGN.md §6's honesty rule pointed outward at the user.
3. THE DOCUMENT IS THE FIXTURE'S, NOT THE MOCK'S. Owner: nobody — it is the conversion, and it
is the reason the copy layer has anything to say. The mock's document body is HTML written
by the mock's author; the build renders Markdown parsed from
app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Control/Authored/capability-documents/trawl/. The fixture
reproduces the mock's document faithfully, so most rows pair by label — but two do not, by
construction, and they are the brief's own constraints rather than an oversight:
the mock's changelog headings carry `available` and
`installed`, and this renderer refuses HTML outright.
4. THE MOCK'S FIGURE IS AN INLINE SVG AND THE BUILD DRAWS AN IMAGE. Owner: nobody. The mock
hand-draws a `<polyline>` sparkline inside a `.figure`; a Markdown document has no way to
express one, and the brief's rule is that an image resolves from inside the downloaded
package. The fixture package therefore carries a real PNG at docs/matches.png and the build
draws it in the same bordered card. The census classifies neither side, so this carries no
finding — recorded because a reader comparing the two will see a different graphic.
5. TWO GEOMETRY VALUES HAVE NO TOKEN BEHIND THEM. Owner: M21 if either is ever authored. The
mock's wide sheet is `min(820px, 94%)` and its body caps at `56vh`. Neither is in DESIGN.md
§2, and arithmetic landing on 820 would be a literal wearing a token's clothes. The build
derives `sidebar * 3` = 768 and `sidebar * 2` = 512. 0 findings: the geometry layer checks
the root against the size it was hosted at and looks for zero-area frames; it does not diff
the mock's pixels.
6. THE MOCK'S BODY LEADING IS OFF DESIGN.md'S LADDER, AND THE LADDER WINS. Owner: nobody.
`.md` sets 13/19 and TypeToken.body is 13/16. SWIFT_PRACTICES.md §5 is that nothing renders
off the eight-role ramp, and DESIGN.md's precedence is that where it and the mock disagree,
the mock is stale. Same for the inline code span's 4px corner: SwiftUI's attributed
`backgroundColor` paints a rectangle and takes no radius, and the alternative is flowing
every paragraph through separate views, which loses the system parser's line breaking.
WHAT IS NOT ENFORCED, stated rather than implied: no layer FAILS on an untagged citation. The
engine reads column four of the pairing as free text. The tag makes the adjudication derivable
from the run's own artifact; it does not make it automatic.

layers.name: font-weight-face
layers.substitute: A SwiftUI Font is opaque — String(describing: Font.system(size: 13, weight: .semibold)) returns "Font(provider: SwiftUI.FontBox<SwiftUI.Font.SystemProvider>)", with no size, weight or face in it. Confirmed instead by: the TypeToken each text node names is recorded in tokens["type"] at apply time and checked against the measured line box by the type-metrics layer; DesignTokenParityTests pins the eight-role ladder against DESIGN.md; scripts/lint/no-raw-design-values.sh fails any font size that does not come off it. None of the three can see an ancestor .font() winning the cascade, and that residue is what this row is.
